## Findings ledger
- [D1.DOC31.F1] Bendix argues that Weber should be read primarily through his empirical investigations because methodological writings and formal definitions do not adequately explain Weber’s substantive analyses — dim: reader_argument — reader-text-year: Reinhard Bendix, 1960 — argument: Weber’s empirical work contains theoretical contributions absent from his methodological writings, while his general definitions do not by themselves explain how he analyzes concrete materials; the reading is meant to answer the problem of how to reconstruct Weber’s sociology as a whole rather than through isolated concepts — role: secondary reader — theme-origin: plan_spine — theme: The historical applicability of estate concepts — position: reconstruction — anchor: "the present study approaches Weber’s work with a major emphasis on his empirical rather than his methodological writings" — doc: em:PL4C6Y9V — anchor-b: "Weber’s methodological writings do not provide an adequate guide to that work because it contains important theoretical contributions that do not appear anywhere else." — doc-b: em:PL4C6Y9V — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes
- [D1.DOC31.F2] Bendix reconstructs Weber’s intellectual perspective as a combination of power-oriented realism and humanistic concern, treating that tension as central to Weber’s sociology and social history — dim: reader_argument — reader-text-year: Reinhard Bendix, 1960 — argument: Weber’s analysis of political and social life is organized around conflict, power and political realism, but is also shaped by commitments to individual value, reason and freedom; this addresses how Weber’s standpoint connects institutional analysis with meaning and political values — role: secondary reader — theme-origin: plan_spine — theme: Marx and Weber as standpoints; meaning, imagined alternatives and class formation — position: consonant — anchor: "Weber gradually developed the same perspective into an image of society and a set of sociological categories" — doc: em:PL4C6Y9V — anchor-b: "Thus, the power-orientation of the educated blended with the humanistic orientation of the powerful" — doc-b: em:PL4C6Y9V — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes

scope_outcomes.criterion: A held secondary text must make an attributable, substantive argument about Max Weber, anchored in its own wording.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected excerpt of Reinhard Bendix’s Max Weber: an intellectual portrait contains explicit interpretive and reconstructive claims about Weber’s empirical method, political sociology, power orientation, humanistic values, comparative sociology and relation between commitment and detachment. Findings F1–F4 record those claims.
limitations: The supplied source is a partial excerpt rather than the complete book.
The excerpt does not settle Bendix’s full treatment of estates, status groups, class, political capitalism or Riley’s work.
No conclusion about Bendix’s silence outside the inspected passages is warranted.
